title: Home Service Booking Rate: Follow Your Last 30 Inquiries
excerpt: Calculate your home service booking rate, trace your last 30 inquiries, and use the worksheet to separate open decisions, lost work, and capacity limits.
angle: Follow the last thirty inquiries to their actual outcomes before changing the marketing budget, with a reusable visual and worksheet.
quick: Count each eligible request once, then divide booked opportunities by eligible inquiries and multiply by 100. Keep pending, declined, no-capacity, and unanswered outcomes separate. Use the last thirty inquiries to choose the next fix, not a universal percentage target.
takeaways: Define eligibility and a booking before calculating the rate.
Count one request once, even when it arrives through several contacts.
Open decisions and no reply yet are not confirmed losses.
Choose the next action from actual outcomes and available capacity.
faqs: How do I calculate my home service booking rate?

Divide booked opportunities by eligible inquiries and multiply by 100. In the fictional example, 12 bookings from 30 eligible inquiries gives 40% so far. Use one row per distinct request and a consistent definition of a booking.
Does a 40% booking rate mean 60% of my marketing spend was wasted?

No. The other inquiries can include customers still deciding, unanswered follow-up, capacity constraints, and declines. Inquiry costs and job values also differ. The percentage alone does not establish wasted spend or lost revenue.
Should missed calls count as eligible inquiries?

Include them when you can establish that the request is for a service you offer in an area you serve. Keep unqualified missed calls in an eligibility-unknown count until you have enough information; do not silently treat them as suitable work or spam.
When should I increase lead spending?

Review suitable inquiry volume, appointment capacity, job mix, acquisition costs, and how existing requests are handled. There is no universal booking-rate threshold that makes more spending appropriate for every business.
How long should I wait before comparing booking rates?

Allow a decision window suited to the work, and use consistent timing when comparing groups. Urgent repairs and planned projects should be reviewed separately. Label an early result as a snapshot while outcomes are still open.
